title: This engineer's pay jumped from $140K to $600K because data centers can't find grid experts
description:
Electricity became the gating factor on AI construction, and the labor market repriced overnight to match. One electrical engineer moved from a consulting firm to a hyperscale data-center owner and watched pay go from roughly $140,000 to more than $600,000, with top candidates drawing signing bonuses between $100,000 and $500,000 in hot markets like Ohio and Texas. The same bottleneck reaches the national ledger: July's widening US trade deficit traces largely to imported servers, chips, and data-center equipment.
A salary that high is a market signal doing exactly what market signals do. It tells people precisely which skill to learn, and power literacy is already being demanded of engineers whose work never touched electricity before. Scarcity priced this loudly tends to fund its own cure, as training programs, tooling, and new entrants chase the gap. The buildout is reorganizing an entire economy around an infrastructure layer that barely existed at this scale a few years ago.
